note: Graded vertical guard of the fast race-cue pilot and its looming TTC governor inside the obstacle stack (visual_brain --obstacle-stack on|shadow; off by default and outside the stack; --vertical-guard off removes it from the stack; shadow computes and logs it without applying it). haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.VerticalGuardConfig. Scale-free: it reads only the looming samples the governor already receives (below_fraction, ttc_lower = the time to contact with the surface fitted below the flight path, the alarm ttc), the measured vertical speed and the pilot's own vertical requests; it uses no height above ground and no metric distance (the only metric bound, gentle_max_m, is a height difference measured by telemetry, as the TTC policy's climb_max_m). Generic and course-agnostic. Versions 1-3 answered the M2 round-2 findings (the governor's fixed 3.5 m/s terrain climb drove three drones into the ~2.2 m Minus Two garage ceiling; the Straw Bale downhill contacts; the Pine Valley mound climb must keep working). Version 4 answers the round-4 live flight minus-fast6-r4-02 (fast PD, guard v3 applied): at 32.35-32.41 s, 0.40-0.44 m above the garage floor and already climbing 0.43-0.51 m/s, two path alarms (alarm 1.14 s, lower TTC 0.43-0.44 s, below_fraction 1.0) started the gentle climb in front of a race arch standing on the floor; the lower window then read the floor and the arch 0.6-1.4 s ahead (below_fraction 0.77-1.0) while the guard's own gentle climb lifted the path toward the arch's top, and version 3 confirmed rising ground at 32.96 s (0.9 m, climbing 0.8 m/s because of the guard, the pilot asking to descend into the arch): 3.5 m/s, overhead cut at 33.26 s, ceiling impact at 34.1 s. Every value of version 3 is kept and none is added; version 4 adds one condition to rule 3's rising-ground confirmation. The live round-4 log minus-fast6-r4-02 (also re-run through looming2 on its recorded frames), the Pine Valley mound of pine-fast6-ttc-01 and the idealised closed-loop check were inspected and replayed while version 4 was designed (development evidence); the other logs of the gates were not replayed with it before this freeze. The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; a change needs a new version and a new freeze before any live flight, and every version is reported. Offline replays of this guard are open loop and are not flight evidence.

vertical_guard_notes.sink_margin: rule 1: the path's crossing TTC with the surface below it, max(alarm ttc, ttc_lower), of the latest sample that has a ttc_lower (aged by the time since its capture, kept memory_s = 1 s after its receipt) scales the pilot's own requested sink by clip((ttc - margin_zero_s) / (margin_full_s - margin_zero_s), 0, 1). Over flat ground both TTCs of a descending path are height / sink rate, so the allowed sink shrinks as the ground approaches (an approach that slows down, not a dive). A surface below the path that the path itself does not head into (a short ttc_lower with a long alarm: the lower window sees ground in front of a ring or an arch opening while the focus of expansion sees through it) limits nothing. The factor falls at up to factor_down_rate (4 /s) and recovers at up to factor_up_rate (1 /s), and the vertical command keeps the pilot's 5 m/s^2 slew, so the request changes without a jump. A requested climb is never scaled
vertical_guard_notes.keep_speed: while the guard withholds part of the pilot's sink, arrests a descent or withholds a terrain climb because the drone descends, and while the pilot's support timers run (the requested sink is not achieved and the drone rests on the terrain below: contact), the descent-path governor's shortfall is not fed, so it does not cut the horizontal request for a sink that was withheld or that the terrain prevents: the drone keeps its speed (throttle up, nose forward) and follows the terrain instead of sinking into it. The guard itself never changes the horizontal request
vertical_guard_notes.descent_first: rule 2: a below-path alarm (below_fraction >= the TTC policy's terrain_fraction 0.7, with the path's crossing TTC, max(alarm ttc, ttc_lower) aged by odometry, under climb_on_s) received while the drone descends (measured vz < -level_band) is the ground looming because the drone descends: the vertical request is held at least level (max(pilot request, 0): never a climb the pilot did not ask for) for arrest_hold_s, brought there at up to arrest_acceleration, and no climb starts. While the drone descends no terrain climb is applied at all (the climb resumes once it is level). On minus-fast6-wall-01 the governor's 3.5 m/s climb started on such a sample (below_fraction 0.78, lower TTC 0.24 s, alarm 0.71 s) while the PD sank at 0.31 m/s
vertical_guard_notes.rising_ground: rule 3: a terrain climb needs confirm (2) below-path alarms (below_fraction >= terrain_fraction 0.7 and ttc_lower aged by odometry under climb_on_s 1.2 s) received while level or climbing within confirm_window_s (0.3 s), and a climb that is not already running starts only if at least one of them is a path alarm: the path's crossing TTC, max(alarm ttc, ttc_lower) aged by odometry, is also under climb_on_s (the flight path itself heads into the surface below it; the same crossing TTC as rules 1 and 2). A surface below the path that the path does not head into (a short ttc_lower with a long alarm: the lower window sees the slope below a crest or below the pilot's line up a hill while the focus of expansion sees over it) starts no climb; it only sustains a running climb (and counts as rising-ground evidence while one runs). The rate is graded by urgency on the below-path TTC (ttc_lower aged by odometry, as the governor ages it): vertical_up (3.5 m/s) x clip((climb_on_s - ttc) / (climb_on_s - climb_full_s), 0, 1), zero at 1.2 s and full at 0.6 s (the sink margin's zero point). Until rising ground is confirmed the climb is bounded to gentle_climb (1 m/s) and to gentle_max_m (1 m) above where the episode began. Rising ground is confirmed by rising_confirm (2) below-path alarms received within rising_window_s (0.5 s) while the drone already climbs faster than rising_min_rise (0.5 m/s, half the gentle climb) and the guard's own climb binds: it exceeds every vertical request the pilot made itself in the last rising_window_s by at least rising_min_rise, so the drone climbs at least rising_min_rise faster because of the guard, and the ground keeps looming although it does, which a floor under a sinking path or a thin structure below the path does not do. A pilot that follows a ring up a hill climbs by its own request, and a brief dip of that request (a checkpoint switch) does not make the guard's climb the reason; alarms then say nothing about the guard's climb being too slow. Then the graded rate applies up to vertical_up, bounded by the TTC policy's climb_max_m (2.5 m). The policy's climb hold (0.5 s) and release (3 m/s^2) are unchanged; so are the ceiling guard (version 3), whose overhead cut still ends any climb under overhead evidence, and its explained (lower-window only) samples, which only sustain a climb, at most gentle_climb. Version 4 adds one condition to the confirmation (rising_ground_v4)
vertical_guard_notes.other_climbs: no other rule of the fast pilot climbs faster than about 1 m/s without the pilot's own evidence: support climb 1 m/s, search 0.5 m/s, the ceiling guard's weak climbs 1 m/s; the launch (1.5 m/s below 0.6 m) and a ring clamped at the top edge ('above', the pilot's own target above) are unchanged
vertical_guard_notes.not_used: the camera process publishes neither the upper window's TTC nor below_fraction_1side, and the logged flights do not carry them; the guard uses the published fields only. On the Straw Bale downhill spots the flight path points below the camera's field of view (looming2's focus of expansion lies below the image; every window is outside it) for the whole approach to each contact, so no looming sample carries below-path evidence there before contact (found by inspecting the offline looming samples and re-running looming2 on the recorded frames of straw-brain08-04, before any replay of this guard): this guard cannot see those contacts coming. It is reported with the replay, not worked around here. Examined for version 4 on its development cases and not used: (1) a test of the lower-window reading against the height gained (the implied height ttc_lower x speed x tan(window depression)), or of its approach rate: in the open-loop replay of the Pine mound the readings lengthened with the recorded 1-1.5 m/s climb at least as much as the garage floor's did, and in the idealised check a ramp's TTC also lengthens while the gentle climb takes effect, then keeps its contact moment; such a test cannot keep the mound's open-loop escalation and, on minus-fast6-r4-02, the arch did approach. (2) An overhead condition (below_fraction at most 0.5 with the alarm under climb_on_s while climbing): at the r4-02 escalation the upper window's urgency (below_fraction 0.77-0.84, U_up 0.24-0.5 /s) was within the range read over the Pine mound's open sky (0.85-0.97, 0.06-0.35 /s); the ceiling became clear only once the escalated climb exceeded 1.5 m/s, and a steep hillside reads about 0.5 as well. (3) A bound on escalated climbs without overhead evidence: during the escalated climbs of r4-02 and of the Pine mound the vertical windows kept evidence (below_fraction known), and a bound on the climb angle that keeps the upper window in view would also cap the mound climb. The ceiling guard (wall-pilot declaration) still cuts climbs under overhead evidence
vertical_guard_notes.rising_ground_v4: rule 3, version 4: rising ground is confirmed (the climb may exceed gentle_climb and gentle_max_m) only when, in addition to version 3's conditions, the surface below kept looming throughout the rising window: no looming sample received in the last rising_window_s (0.5 s) before the confirming alarm saw the surface below the path farther than climb_on_s (1.2 s), that is a lower-surface TTC, aged by odometry, of at least climb_on_s, or no lower-surface TTC although the vertical windows had evidence (below_fraction known: the lower window saw no crossing). A sample without vertical-window evidence says nothing either way. This is version 3's own premise ('the ground keeps looming although the drone climbs') made strict, with version 3's values. A surface misread below the path at low height (the lower-window reading flickers with the attitude and grows with the height), or a structure the climb is already clearing, gives such readings while the gentle climb runs: the gentle climb was enough at that moment, so it is not escalated. Rising ground that the gentle climb does not clear keeps every reading under climb_on_s. A reading that stays under climb_on_s for rising_window_s is still escalated as in version 3, whatever surface produced it

change: v4 (after the round-4 live flights of guard v3 on Minus Two, before any replay of v4 except the development cases named in note; every value, rules 1, 2 and keep speed are v3's): rule 3's rising-ground confirmation also needs no looming sample in the last rising_window_s that saw the surface below the path farther than climb_on_s (a lower-surface TTC of climb_on_s or more, or none with below_fraction known). Diagnosis of minus-fast6-r4-02 (development): the gentle climb began at 32.42 s on two path alarms received while the PD already climbed 0.43-0.51 m/s 0.40-0.44 m above the floor (alarm 1.14 s, lower 0.43-0.44 s, below_fraction 1.0); looming2 re-run on the recorded frames (18 fps) shows the lower window on the floor, with a visual rotation correction of 5.5 deg at the onset (0.2-3 deg over the next 0.7 s), and a race arch standing on the floor 5-7 m ahead. During the gentle climb (vz 0.8-0.95 m/s, 32.5-32.9 s) the lower window read the floor and the arch 0.60-1.41 s ahead (below_fraction 0.77-1.0), two readings at or above climb_on_s (1.34 s at 32.54 s, 1.41 s at 32.77 s), while the alarm read 1.40-1.69 s through the arch; the guard's climb bound by 0.52 m/s over the pilot's requests once the pilot's 0.53 m/s left the rising window, and v3 confirmed rising ground at 32.96 s in the log (at 32.90 s in the open-loop replay, on the alarms of 32.84 s and 32.90 s, lower 0.68 and 0.90 s, at 0.84 m): 3.5 m/s from 33.0 s. The upper window then read the ceiling (below_fraction 0.84, 0.77, 0.46, 0.32, 0.28 at 32.96-33.16 s; alarm 0.83-1.25 s); the ceiling guard cut the climb at 33.26 s (1.42 m, climbing 2.4 m/s) and the request reached 0 at 33.41 s with 1.8-2.0 m/s still measured: impact at (73.5, 69.4, 2.13), 34.1 s. Every one of v3's escalation attempts there had, in the 0.5 s before it, a sample that saw the surface below farther than climb_on_s; on the Pine mound (pine-fast6-ttc-01, 4.09-4.56 s) no sample read more than 0.67 s. Two other conditions were tried on these development cases before this freeze and dropped (see vertical_guard_notes.not_used): an approach-rate test of the predicted contact moment (it held the idealised ramps at the gentle climb and blocked r4-02 only on one low reading) and an overhead condition (no effect on either case; a steep hillside reads like it).
